subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a global CLI agent dry-run mode that intercepts every tool call, or should safe preview behavior stay scoped to owner commands and broader safe workflow modes?
rationale: The requested behavior changes the safety contract for built-in, plugin, client, bundle MCP, and native harness tools; automation can show the gap, but maintainers need to choose the product/security semantics before code lands.

options.title: Design global agent dry-run
options.body: Approve a core CLI agent mode with explicit semantics for hooks, approvals, audit, read-only tools, plugin/client tools, native harnesses, stderr/stdout, and structured model responses.

options.title: Keep dry-run scoped
options.body: Continue adding dry-run previews only to owner commands such as doctor, update, cron, config, or skills where side effects and preview payloads are easier to define.

options.title: Fold into safe workflow modes
options.body: Track this under a broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent-mode design and avoid a narrow global flag until that direction is settled.

recommendation.title: Design global agent dry-run
recommendation.body: Approve a core CLI agent mode with explicit semantics for hooks, approvals, audit, read-only tools, plugin/client tools, native harnesses, stderr/stdout, and structured model responses.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the major agent runtime refactor and recent maintenance on the central agent/tool execution path.
